ios.decoder: Foundation.JSONDecoder, default key strategy (match by member name)

website.decoder: Response.json(), structurally tolerant (every read is guarded)

transport.methods: Any. No route restricts the HTTP method; GET and POST return identical bodies and HEAD returns the headers with an empty body.
transport.host_routing: The Host header selects the website via websiteMiddleware. An unmatched Host falls back to DefaultWebsite, which is the first website returned by the config provider unless some website has an empty hostname. There is no 404-on-unknown-Host.
transport.compression: gorilla/handlers.CompressHandler wraps every route, so every response carries Vary: Accept-Encoding and is gzipped when the client asks.
transport.debug_header: RW-Debug: 1 switches the GORM log level to Info for /span, /snow and /forecast. It does not change the response.

query.name: station
query.note: Required. 400 if absent, 404 if it is not a configured device name.

query.name: station_id
query.note: Accepted by both clients but IGNORED by this handler: only `station` selects data.

query.name: format
query.note: NOT honoured here -- /span encodes with json.NewEncoder directly, not through the formatter.

statuses.400: `station parameter is required`, `error: invalid span duration`, or `time span exceeds maximum allowed duration of 1 year` -- plain text, trailing newline.
statuses.500: `error fetching weather data` or `database not enabled`.
statuses.503: JSON {error, message} when no website resolves.

headers.Cache-Control: max-age=<data interval in seconds minus 1, default 60>

endpoints.aggregate_source: span <= 6h -> weather_1m; <= 48h -> weather_5m; <= 14d -> weather_1h; else weather_1d.

query.name: station_id
query.note: Preferred form. 400 on a non-integer, 404 on an unknown id.

query.name: station
query.note: Legacy form. 404 on an unknown name.

statuses.404: `station not found`, or `no recent weather data available for this station` when the newest reading for the station is older than 10 minutes.
statuses.500: `error fetching weather data` or `database not enabled`.
statuses.503: JSON {error, message} when no website resolves.

notes: Neither parameter given: the website's primary device is used.
The 10-minute recency window is the only place in the contract where staleness becomes a 404.

statuses.200: A single JSON object. All zeros when the gauge has never reported.
statuses.404: `snow data not enabled for this website` (website snow_enabled false), or `station not found`.
statuses.500: `error fetching readings from DB`, `error encoding snow data`, `database not enabled`.
statuses.503: JSON {error, message} when no website resolves.

notes: The iOS client sends NO query parameters at all; the website sends station_id.
station/station_id only redirect the depth lookup. stationname and all six totals come from the website's configured snow_device_name regardless.
There is NO recency filter on the depth query, so an offline gauge keeps returning its last known depth indefinitely.

statuses.200: JSON object; `{}` when the station has no cached extremes.
statuses.500: `error querying almanac data` or `database not enabled`.

notes: Every field is omitempty, so absent metrics are absent keys, never nulls.
Air-quality extremes are read from the website's air_quality_device, not from `station`.
Snow extremes (deepest_snow, max_snow_hour, max_snow_day) are never populated: handlers.go:1416 disables them.

endpoints.grammar: /forecast/<1 to 4 digits>  (regex ^\d{1,4}$). The value is forecast_span_hours, not a duration: 24 is the hourly forecast, 240 the ten-day one.
endpoints.registered_when: at least one device has aeris_enabled; otherwise the route does not exist (404 from the file server)

query.name: period
query.note: Replaces the data array with the single element at that index -- an OBJECT, not an array.

statuses.400: Empty body when the span fails the regex; a JSON error body served as text/plain for a bad `period`.
statuses.404: EMPTY body, no Content-Type, when no forecast record matches.
statuses.500: `error encoding forecast data` or `database not enabled`.

notes: lastUpdated is Go's time.Time.String() -- `2006-01-02 15:04:05.999999999 -0700 MST`, NOT RFC3339. weather-utils.js parses it with moment format `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss.SSSSSS-ZZ`.
The response is NOT newline-terminated: WriteRawJSON writes bytes rather than using json.Encoder.
`data` is Postgres jsonb written back verbatim, so key order is jsonb-normalised (key length, then bytewise) and the numeric text is whatever was stored -- `0.0`, not `0`.
The 18 period fields come from json.Marshal of []AerisWeatherForecastPeriod in internal/controllers/aerisweather/controller.go, so the shape is server-controlled, not Aeris-controlled.

endpoints.registered_when: at least one device has aeris_enabled

statuses.400: `station_id parameter is required` or `invalid station_id parameter`.

notes: Active alerts only: begins_at <= now AND expires_at > now, ordered begins_at DESC.
No shipped client reads this endpoint. The website JS never references it.

endpoints.grammar: / exactly (gorilla/mux HandleFunc, so /latest/ and other trailing-slash paths fall through to the file server and 404)
notes: A portal website serves portal.html.tmpl here instead.
No Cache-Control header is set.

Content-Type has NO charset, unlike the static JS the file server returns (text/javascript; charset=utf-8). A client that string-matches the content type would see two different values for two .js URLs on the same site.
This is the one deliberate exception to carrying the website forward as-is (DESIGN D-38).

statuses.404: `404 page not found` on a non-portal website.

notes: portal.html.tmpl consumes NO template variables at all; PageTitle is passed and ignored.

endpoints.handler: handlers.go ServePrivacy (static file, not a template)
notes: Served for EVERY website, including portals, and before any website check -- it is the only route that works with no website configured.

statuses.403: `stations API not available for this website` on a non-portal website.
statuses.500: `error loading station data` / `error loading website data` / `error encoding stations`.

notes: Devices with latitude == 0 AND longitude == 0 are excluded.
Disabled devices ARE included, with enabled: false.
The nested `website` object is present only for devices bound to a non-portal website that has a hostname.

response.type: array of RemoteStationResponse (declared inside the handler)

statuses.403: `remote stations API not available for this website`.
statuses.500: `error loading remote station data`, including when any text column of a remote_stations row is NULL -- the scan into a Go string fails.

notes: status is derived from last_seen: < 5 min online, < 30 min stale, else offline.
No shipped client reads this. The only in-repo consumer is the management UI, which fetches `/api/remote-stations` relative to the management server, where no such route exists.

statuses.500: `error loading station data` or `error encoding station info`.

notes: Takes no parameters: the website is selected entirely by the Host header.
`stations` lists every device with a location, enabled or not, including the snow gauge and the air-quality monitor. The iOS client filters those out client-side.
This is the only endpoint carrying a live compatibility hazard -- see `hazards`.

response.type: per-file, from Go's mime sniffing (font/ttf, font/woff2, image/svg+xml, ...)

statuses.200: File bytes, or a directory listing for /fonts/ itself.

statuses.200: File bytes, or a directory listing for a directory path.

quirks.summary: `ohum` and `outhumidity` are the same measurement, emitted twice.
quirks.detail: transform.go sets both OutHumidity and OutsideHumidity from r.OutHumidity. The website reads `ohum`; the iOS client decodes both. Neither may be dropped.

quirks.summary: Field naming is inconsistent and must stay that way.
quirks.detail: `otemp`, `bar`, `winds`, `windd`, `itemp`, `ihum`, `windch`, `heatidx` are run together; `period_rain` is snake_case; `moonPhaseName`, `moonIllumination`, `moonAge`, `moonCrescentAngle` are camelCase; everything else is lower-concatenated.

quirks.summary: `ts` is milliseconds since the Unix epoch as a JSON integer.
quirks.detail: transform.go uses UnixMilli() on Timestamp for /latest and on Bucket for /span. Go emits it as a bare integer (Int64), 13 digits at present. Swift decodes it as Int64.

quirks.summary: `snowdepth` is MILLIMETRES on /latest and INCHES on /snow and /span.
quirks.detail: fetchLatestReading selects (base_distance - snowdistance) in mm and transformLatestReadings passes it through unconverted; transformSpanReadings and GetSnowLatest both apply mmToInchesWithThreshold. Same key, same endpoint family, two units.

quirks.summary: `windcard` carries omitempty but is never absent.
quirks.detail: headingToCardinalDirection always returns one of sixteen non-empty strings, including for a wind direction of 0 (`N`), so the key is always present in practice.

quirks.summary: /span never populates windgust, rainfall24h/48h/72h or rainfallstorm.
quirks.detail: transformSpanReadings does not set them, and they have no omitempty, so every /span element carries them as 0. Only /latest computes them.

quirks.summary: /span overwrites extrafloat1 with a smoothed snow-depth estimate for snow stations.
quirks.detail: fetchWeatherSpan joins snow_depth_est_5m and writes snow_depth_est_in into ExtraFloat1 when the station has a base snow distance. The same key means PM1.0 on an AirGradient device. SnowResponse.swift documents this ('Optional because /snow doesn't include them, but /span does').

quirks.summary: /snow reports the website's snow device name even when another station was queried.
quirks.detail: stationname is always website.SnowDeviceName; `station`/`station_id` only redirect the depth lookup. Querying /snow?station=<a weather station> yields that station's (absent) depth under the snow gauge's name, with the snow gauge's totals.

quirks.summary: A gap in /span data is simply missing buckets.
quirks.detail: The continuous aggregates produce no row for a bucket with no readings, and the handler does not gap-fill, so the ts sequence jumps. Clients must not assume a constant interval.

quirks.summary: Bad-`period` errors on /forecast are JSON bodies labelled text/plain.
quirks.detail: w.WriteHeader(400) runs before formatter.WriteResponse, so Go has already committed the sniffed Content-Type. The body is valid JSON; the header says otherwise.

quirks.summary: Three /forecast failure modes return a completely empty body and no Content-Type.
quirks.detail: A span failing the 1-to-4-digit regex, a span with no record, and a station name with no device all call w.WriteHeader(...) and return. Content-Length is 0 and there is no Content-Type header.

quirks.summary: Hand-encoded endpoints end with a newline; /forecast does not.
quirks.detail: json.NewEncoder(w).Encode appends '\n'. /forecast goes through WriteRawJSON, which writes the jsonb bytes with no terminator. This is a real byte-level difference.

quirks.summary: Go emits `0`, not `0.0`, for a zero float32; jsonb passthrough emits whatever was stored.
quirks.detail: encoding/json uses the shortest round-tripping representation, so 0 is `0`, 57.0 is `57`, 23.730469 is `23.730469`. /forecast's `data` is Postgres jsonb text, which preserves the numeric literal as written -- the same contract therefore contains both `0` and `0.0`.

quirks.summary: `format=msgpack` is a parallel encoding of the same contract, and loses number types.
quirks.detail: responseformat.Formatter switches to vmihailenco/msgpack with SetCustomStructTag("json"), so the key names match. For /forecast it decodes the jsonb into interface{} first, so every number becomes a float64. /span does NOT honour the parameter at all. No shipped client sends it.

quirks.summary: `/span` is 500, not 200, for a station whose winddir is NULL in the window.
quirks.detail: circular_avg_final divides by the accumulator, which stays 0 when the aggregate saw no non-NULL winddir, so the aggregate query fails with SQLSTATE 22012. The shipping Go daemon never writes NULL -- it inserts its whole reading struct, zeros included -- so the bug is latent today. It becomes live for any writer that leaves unpopulated metrics NULL.
quirks.evidence: reproduced during capture; see docs/legacy-api-contract.md section 8

quirks.summary: `/api/remote-stations` is 500 for a remote_stations row with any NULL text column.
quirks.detail: The row is scanned into Go strings, and `converting NULL to string is unsupported` surfaces as `error loading remote station data`.
quirks.evidence: reproduced during capture; see docs/legacy-api-contract.md section 8

quirks.summary: Every endpoint accepts every HTTP method.
quirks.detail: No route calls .Methods(...). POST /latest returns the same body as GET. HEAD returns headers with an empty body.
quirks.evidence: probed during capture; see docs/legacy-api-contract.md section 1

quirks.summary: An unknown Host silently serves the first configured website.
quirks.detail: websiteMiddleware falls back to DefaultWebsite, set to the first website the config provider returns unless one has an empty hostname. Nothing distinguishes 'wrong host' from 'right host'.
quirks.evidence: probed during capture; see docs/legacy-api-contract.md section 1

quirks.summary: Almanac snow metrics are permanently absent.
quirks.detail: deepest_snow, max_snow_hour and max_snow_day are declared in AlmanacData but never assigned; handlers.go:1416 carries `Snow metrics temporarily disabled due to performance issues`. The keys are omitempty, so they simply never appear.

quirks.summary: Directory listings are served for the asset trees.
quirks.detail: http.FileServer renders an HTML index for /js/, /css/, /images/ and /fonts/. Whether the Rust implementation reproduces that is a decision, not an accident -- record it either way.
quirks.evidence: probed during capture; see docs/legacy-api-contract.md section 6
